outcome: Help educators design valid assessments and investigate integrity concerns consistently under human control.
overview: Assessment design and integrity review are labour-intensive and inconsistent across programmes, exposing institutions to invalid measurement and disputed decisions. This solution checks curriculum alignment, coverage, difficulty, accessibility and question reuse in assessment blueprints, and assembles evidence packs for suspected integrity cases — it never makes a misconduct or grade decision. Flagged cases always route to a named academic authority, with a complete evidence chain and appeal trail. A pilot across one assessment cycle targets a 25% reduction in moderation time while meeting the institution’s validity and accessibility rubric, with 100% of integrity findings adjudicated by humans.

benefits.text: Reduce assessment moderation time by a target 25% within one assessment cycle
benefits.source: Redington Education catalogue; to validate against the current moderation baseline
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Depends on blueprint and item-bank quality — not a guarantee

benefits.text: Strengthen assessment validity — better curriculum coverage and fewer weak or duplicated questions
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Measured against the institution’s own validity rubric during the pilot

benefits.text: Make integrity investigations defensible — consistent evidence packs, human adjudication, full appeal trail
benefits.source: Reference design — evidence chain and appeal records are structural
benefits.limits: The system prepares evidence; it does not and cannot prove misconduct

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (UAE, KSA); assessment items and case evidence stay in the institution’s tenancy in the reference designs

notFor.situation: The institution wants automated cheating detection or automated grading decisions
notFor.why: The design prohibits autonomous misconduct or grade decisions — it prepares evidence for named humans

notFor.situation: No defined assessment policy, moderation workflow or appeal process
notFor.why: The tooling enforces and accelerates an existing governance process; it cannot substitute for one

scope:
Model: Joint delivery: accredited implementation partner leads, with Redington architecture and commercial governance; the institution owns assessment policy, grading authority and adjudication · Duration: 6–10 weeks setup and pilot; 12–20 weeks to production
Delivery pod: Partner delivery lead + project manager, assessment analyst, security engineer; customer assessment director, faculty moderators, integrity officer, accessibility lead · Support model: Business-hours support with assessment-period escalation cover; severity-based response targets; partner service desk with vendor escalation
1) Policy mapping and rubric configuration
2) Item-bank and evidence integration
3) Reviewer workflow co-design
4) Security and access testing
5) Cycle pilot with double-review sampling
6) Cycle review and benefit report

Appeal trail proven; reviewer UAT complete
